Its separate list of Presidents and Chairs carries the entry '2002-2003 Bryce Zabel Chair/CEO' independently.

The Television Academy credits Zabel with creating five primetime network series including the 'Emmy-winning Dark Skies (NBC)', alongside Kay O'Brien, M.A.N.T.I.S., The Crow: Stairway to Heaven and E.N.G.

label: Bryce Zabel
narrative: Bryce Zabel matters to this board for one specific reason: he is the person who systematically worked through what happens after disclosure, rather than whether it will occur. With Richard Dolan he co-authored A.D. (After Disclosure), which treats the end of the secret as a governance and social-order problem - who is prosecuted, what happens to markets and religions, how a state that lied for eighty years re-legitimates itself. That is the question the legislative strand keeps colliding with and never answers. Zabel's professional background is unusual for the field: a University of Oregon broadcast journalism graduate and former CNN correspondent who became a television showrunner, created the UFO-conspiracy series Dark Skies in 1996, and in 2001 was elected chairman and CEO of the Academy of Television Arts and Sciences. Dark Skies is itself an artefact worth noting - a prime-time dramatisation of a Majestic-12-style control group broadcast in 1996, which is either prescient or evidence of how long the structural narrative has been in circulation.
